# Tacto Negotiation Arena - starter kit For team experiments and the final, use [the arena-harness CLI](HARNESS.md): local simulation by default, plugin agents, durable recovery, budgets and comparable reports. A Python client for the arena API, two example buyer agents that negotiate by e-mail, helpers that read the suppliers' documents and price a term sheet, a runner that plays many cases in parallel, `arena-sim` - a local simulator of the arena's API - and a read-only MCP server over the data package. Read the brief first (`../brief/brief.md`); the full API is in `../brief/api.md`. Code: MIT. ## Quickstart - first agent on the board in 15 minutes You need Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). **1. Get your team's key** (one per team): open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a contact e-mail, and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once an organiser approves, the key appears **once** on that page - copy it and press "Got the key". Only that page (or its link) shows it; lost it → ask the organisers to reset it. Keep it out of git. ```bash cd starter-kit uv sync --all-extras # 2. install cp .env.example .env # 3. put ARENA_URL and your key (ARENA_API_KEY) into .env uv run arena me # 4. your team and its practice quota uv run arena cases # 5. the practice cases (the 10 hosted ones are playable) uv run arena play case:P01 -v # 6. the naive agent negotiates one case uv run arena board # 7. you are on the practice leaderboard ``` Is the arena up? `curl $ARENA_URL/health`. Step 6 prints the deal, your total cost `c_deal` against `c_open` and `c_best`, the case score, and a **replay link**: every e-mail and the supplier's reasons for each move, in words. That is the learning loop - play a practice case, read the replay, improve your agent, play again. In practice your best score per case counts, so play a case again whenever your agent improves. **Quota:** 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours. `arena play` and `arena run` print how many are left; `arena run` plays only the hosted practice cases and stops starting new ones once the quota is used up (a `429` there does not go away by retrying). Plan your runs. **Now the LLM agent.** Download the data (`ARENA_DATA=data/package` in `.env`), choose a model in `.env` (your own key), then: ```bash uv run arena data # unpacks data/package (and the Sunday release once public) uv run arena play case:P01 --agent llm -v uv run arena run --set practice --agent llm --parallel 8 # every hosted practice case, 8 at a time uv run arena play case:D02 -v # the sandbox: 3 demo suppliers, no board ``` **Sunday 08:00:** run `arena data` again - it adds `data/release-sunday` (new news, letters, a memo). `DataPackage` merges its facts and documents automatically; hidden cases may cite them. ## Hello World (local, 3 commands) No key yet? Play a whole case against the local simulator - no network, no quota, no LLM costs. The simulator's supplier is a plain script; the real ones are on arena.tacto.ai. After `uv sync --all-extras` (step 2 above): ```bash # terminal 1: the simulator (--data is optional: leave it out until you have run `arena data`) uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package # terminal 2: a simulator key, then the naive agent plays case:S01 ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Hello World" sim # prints an api_key ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 ARENA_API_KEY= uv run arena play case:S01 -v ``` It prints the deal, `c_deal` against `c_open` and `c_best`, the score and a replay link - open it in your browser: the result on top, then every e-mail of the negotiation. ## Try it by hand (Postman, curl) Feel the API before you put a model in front of it. On the real arena (practice and sandbox) the 60-second rule applies: three late replies in a row end the thread - too fast for typing. **By hand, use the simulator first**, without the clock: ```bash uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package # data/package from `arena data`; --data is optional ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Team Name" sim # prints a simulator api_key export SIM=http://127.0.0.1:8000 KEY= ``` Every call sends `X-API-Key: `; every `POST` also `Content-Type: application/json` and a fresh `X-Move-Id` (any unique string - the same id again returns the same answer). In Postman: those headers, the body as raw JSON. ```bash # 1. the cases: case:S01 has one supplier, sup:70270, and the negotiable fields unit_price, payment_days curl -s "$SIM/v1/cases?set=practice" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" # 2. open a session: the reply carries session_id (sim1 on a fresh simulator) and each supplier's quote e-mail curl -s -X POST "$SIM/v1/sessions" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-Move-Id: open-1" -d '{"case_id": "case:S01"}' # 3. the supplier's opening e-mail: its term sheet (offer:70270-0) and the quote PDF to fetch curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" # 4. your e-mail with an offer: the reply is the supplier's answer (status, term_sheets, claim_results) curl -s -X POST "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270/messages" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Move-Id: msg-1" \ -d '{"message": {"subject": "Adapter piece HI", "body": "Thank you for your quote. We offer 15.50 EUR at 60 days.", "term_sheets": [{"terms": {"unit_price": 15.5, "payment_days": 60}}]}}' # 5. read the reply in the thread, and the session state curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" ``` To close, send `{"message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": "offer:70270-1"}}}` (the term sheet you take) or `{"message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}}` to the same `messages` path; the answer carries the result and score. The quote PDF: `GET $SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/attachments/att:70270-0-quote`. The same calls work on the arena (`https://arena.tacto.ai`, your team's key, a practice case) - with the clock running. ## The Live Final: waves, in parallel, within the cap The final comes in 5 themed waves. A wave holds several hidden cases that appear when the host starts it; play them all in parallel (up to 10 open sessions per key). Each wave has a hard cap - **8 minutes** (the host may extend one) - and what is still open then ends without a deal. Start the runner before the first wave and leave it running: ```bash uv run arena run --set final --agent llm --parallel 10 ``` It polls `GET /v1/cases?set=final`, plays every case of a new wave at once (one agent per case), closes each case **90 seconds before its wave's cap** (read from the wave's `seconds_left`, so an extension counts) - earlier if a round in that case took longer (`play.closing_move`: the cheapest standing term sheet that keeps the must-haves and beats your alternative, else walk away) and stops after the fifth wave has closed. If it crashes, start it again: it picks up the sessions it had started. In Python: `play_waves(client, new_agent)`. It reads only your own cases and sessions - during the final your agent must not read the leaderboard, the screen or the event feed (`arena board` is for you, not for the agent). A supplier's reply can take up to about a minute; its time never counts against your 60 seconds, and the client waits up to 180 seconds for a reply. The client paces itself below the limit of 10 calls per second and retries dropped connections with the same `X-Move-Id`, so a retry never sends a message twice. Rehearse with `arena run --set practice --parallel 10` (it counts against your quota) before Sunday, from the machine and network you will use: every case should end well inside 8 minutes. ## Your own agent An agent is any object with `decide(case, threads) -> {"supplier_id": …, "message": {…}}`. `threads` holds every e-mail so far per supplier, oldest first; supplier attachments come with their text under `"text"`. The message is an e-mail - subject, body, up to 3 term sheets - or an action that closes the case: ```python from arena_kit import ArenaClient, RemoteTable, complete_offer, play, total_cost from arena_kit.docs import standard_terms from arena_kit.play import latest, live_threads, standing class Haggler: def decide(self, case, threads): sid = live_threads(threads)[0] events = threads[sid] sheet_id, terms = standing(events) # the supplier's standing term sheet std = standard_terms(events) # from its quote PDF: what closes if a field is missing if latest(events)["status"] in ("agreed", "final_offer"): return { "supplier_id": sid, "message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": sheet_id}}, } ask = complete_offer(case, {**terms, "unit_price": terms["unit_price"] * 0.97}) print("their C:", total_cost(case, terms, std), "ours:", total_cost(case, ask)) return { "supplier_id": sid, "message": { "subject": case["title"], "body": "Thank you for your quote. Could you send us a cost breakdown?", "term_sheets": [{"terms": ask}], }, } print(play(RemoteTable(ArenaClient()), "case:P01", Haggler())) ``` | Module | What | |---|---| | `client.py` | `ArenaClient`: one method per endpoint (messages, threads, attachments, back office, `me`, ...); paced, safe retries; `practice_remaining` | | `play.py` | `play()`, `play_all()`, `play_waves()` (the Live Final); `RemoteTable` - the hosted arena (practice, sandbox, final) | | `cost.py` | the published cost function C with the category goal's rates, `supplier_value` for the relationship term, must-haves, term-sheet completion | | `docs.py` | supplier documents to text (PDF, XLSX); a quote PDF to its offered, standard and fixed terms | | `data.py` | the data package and the Sunday release: `facts.json`, read-only SQL, lookup by ID, documents, cases | | `agents/naive.py` | anchors 10 % low, splits the difference, accepts early - the baseline | | `agents/llm.py` | the model writes the e-mail and the term sheets from the case and the data it points to; code computes C, reads the documents, removes IDs that do not exist, and refuses bad accepts | | `sim.py` | `arena-sim`: the public API on your machine, with one plain scripted supplier (below) | | `mcp_server.py` | the MCP server below | The LLM agent is a starting point, not a winner: it sees only what the case file points to. Finding the data that moves a supplier is your job - the worked example below shows one way for one kind of argument. Ideas beyond it: mine the notes and e-mails, read the suppliers' signals and documents, send two or three term sheets to learn what a supplier values, ask its roles the right questions, keep RFQ threads alive in parallel, and never leak urgency, a budget or a missing alternative. **Strategic and bottleneck cases** (`category_goal` `stabilise` or `secure_supply`) charge C for a deal that leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin. Pass your estimate of the supplier to price it - without one, `total_cost` leaves the term out: ```python supplier = {"full_cost": 128.0, "interest_rate": 0.12, "standard": std} # your estimate total_cost(case, terms, std, supplier) ``` ## Worked example: cite an index (case P01) Brandlhuber, a foundry, announces +9.5 % on volute casings and blames energy and wages. Does the data agree? `DataPackage` reads the package (the MCP server below gives an LLM the same access): ```python from arena_kit.data import DataPackage pkg = DataPackage("data/package") # 1. What drives this part's cost? The category team's estimate: pkg.query("SELECT series_id, weight FROM cost_drivers WHERE part_id = 'part:310010'") # -> PPI-C241 (iron and steel) 0.26, PPI-D351 (electric power) 0.06, LCI-C (labour) 0.32 # 2. The letter blames energy: read the electricity producer price index for the last year. rows = pkg.query( "SELECT id, month, value FROM index_values WHERE series_id = 'PPI-D351' AND month >= '2025-08' ORDER BY month" ) # 3. Compute the change yourself - two months of one series, at most 12 months apart, # ending within the last 12 months of the data. a, b = rows[0], rows[-1] change = (b["value"] / a["value"] - 1) * 100 # 4. One sentence: the figure next to both IDs. print(f"Electricity producer prices changed {change:+.1f}% from {a['month']} to {b['month']} ({a['id']}, {b['id']}).") # -> Electricity producer prices changed -3.7% from 2025-08 to 2026-08 # (idx:PPI-D351@2025-08, idx:PPI-D351@2026-08). ``` Put that sentence into your e-mail and read `claim_results` in the reply: `verified` (the figure matches the data), `irrelevant` (true, but not about this supplier's costs, or the window is too old) or `contradicted` (a wrong figure - it costs trust). Whether it moves the price, and how far, is the supplier's business - a true figure may disarm one supplier and leave the next cold; the replay shows what it made of it. Which series matter to which supplier, which window, and what else in the data speaks for you - that is up to your agent. """Copy this file to my_agent.py and run --agent my_agent. No API plumbing needed.""" from arena_kit.harness.plugins import Baseline class Agent(Baseline): def prepare(self, context): # context: case and TOML [parameters]. Return JSON state. return {"decisions": 0} def decide(self, observation, state, services): # services.data.query/lookup/document; services.cost; services.complete(messages). state = {**state, "decisions": state["decisions"] + 1} return super().decide(observation, state, services) agent = "baseline" parallel = 10 decision_seconds = 30 max_cases = 1 poll_seconds = 5 [parameters] "}}

"""Read-only access to the data package: SQL, lookup by citable ID, documents, practice cases -
plus the Sunday release (new news, letters and a memo) once you have downloaded it."""

import csv
import json
import os
import sqlite3
from functools import cached_property
from pathlib import Path

MAX_ROWS = 200
RELEASE = "release-sunday"


class DataPackage:
    def __init__(self, root, release=None):
        """`root`: the unpacked package. `release`: the unpacked Sunday release (default: a
        `release-sunday` folder inside or next to the package, or ARENA_RELEASE), if present."""
        self.root = Path(root).expanduser().resolve()
        # facts.json holds every citable fact with the fields the arena checks claims against.
        own = self.root / "facts.json"
        facts = [own] if own.is_file() else [p for p in sorted(self.root.rglob("facts.json")) if RELEASE not in p.parts]
        self.facts = json.loads(facts[0].read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if facts else {}
        release = release or os.environ.get("ARENA_RELEASE")
        candidates = [Path(release).expanduser()] if release else [self.root / RELEASE, self.root.parent / RELEASE]
        self.release = next((p.resolve() for p in candidates if (p / "facts.json").is_file()), None)
        if self.release:  # new IDs only: nothing in the package changes
            self.facts |= json.loads((self.release / "facts.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        dbs = sorted(self.root.rglob("*.sqlite")) + sorted(self.root.rglob("*.db"))
        if not dbs and not facts:
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"no facts.json or .sqlite under {self.root}")
        self.db = None
        if dbs:
            self.db = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{dbs[0]}?mode=ro", uri=True, check_same_thread=False)
            self.db.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
            self.db.execute("PRAGMA query_only = ON")

    def tables(self):
        """{table: {"columns": [...], "rows": n}}"""
        if self.db is None:
            return {}
        names = [r[0] for r in self.db.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' ORDER BY name")]
        return {
            t: {
                "columns": [f"{c[1]} {c[2]}".strip() for c in self.db.execute(f'PRAGMA table_info("{t}")')],
                "rows": self.db.execute(f'SELECT count(*) FROM "{t}"').fetchone()[0],
            }
            for t in names
        }

    def query(self, sql, params=(), limit=MAX_ROWS):
        if self.db is None:
            raise ValueError("this package has no SQLite file")
        if sql.lstrip().split(None, 1)[0].lower() not in {"select", "with"}:
            raise ValueError("read-only: SELECT or WITH statements only")
        cur = self.db.execute(sql, params)
        return [dict(r) for r in cur.fetchmany(limit)]

    @cached_property
    def _ids(self):
        # A table's citable ID sits in its `id` column, else in its first column.
        index = {}
        for t, meta in self.tables().items():
            cols = [c.split()[0] for c in meta["columns"]]
            key = "id" if "id" in cols else cols[0]
            for row in self.db.execute(f'SELECT * FROM "{t}"'):
                value = row[key]
                if isinstance(value, str) and ":" in value:
                    index[value] = {"table": t, **dict(row)}
        for path in sorted(self.release.glob("data/*.csv")) if self.release else []:  # not in the SQLite
            with path.open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
                for row in csv.DictReader(f):
                    index[row["id"]] = {"table": path.stem, **row, "root": str(self.release)}
        return index

    def lookup(self, ref):
        """The fact behind a citable ID (from facts.json, else its table row), or None."""
        return self.facts.get(ref) or self._ids.get(ref)

    def ids(self, prefix):
        """All citable IDs starting with `prefix`, sorted, e.g. ids("idx:GP19-245113@")."""
        return sorted(i for i in self.facts.keys() | self._ids.keys() if i.startswith(prefix))

    def document(self, ref):
        """A document's text by ID (row with a path or body column) or by path in the package."""
        row, base = self._ids.get(ref) or self.facts.get(ref), self.root
        if row:
            for col in ("body", "text", "content"):
                if row.get(col):
                    return row[col]
            base = Path(row.get("root") or self.root)
            ref = next((row[c] for c in ("path", "file") if row.get(c)), None)
            if ref is None:
                return json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False)
        path = (base / ref).resolve()
        if not path.is_relative_to(base) or not path.is_file():
            raise FileNotFoundError(ref)
        return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    @cached_property
    def cases(self):
        """Practice (and demo) case files in the package: {case_id: case}."""
        out = {}
        for p in sorted(self.root.rglob("cases/**/*.json")):
            case = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            if isinstance(case, dict) and "case_id" in case:
                out[case["case_id"]] = case
        return out

# Optional estimates only; enter your provider's actual prices.

# arena-sim as a container:  docker build -t arena-sim starter-kit && docker run -p 8080:8080 arena-sim

ENV UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1 UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=never

COPY arena_kit ./arena_kit
RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-editable --extra sim && useradd --create-home sim
USER sim

CMD ["sh", "-c", "exec /app/.venv/bin/arena-sim serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port ${PORT}"]

## Offline: arena-sim, the contract simulator

```bash

```

`arena register` exists for the simulator only: it hands out its own keys, which work nowhere
else. The arena's key comes from `/apply` (step 1).

`arena-sim` speaks the arena's public API exactly - paths, fields, statuses, error codes, limits,
the 60-second rule, quote PDFs and cost-breakdown XLSX files in the arena's format, RFQs with
parallel threads, leaderboard and replay JSON - with three example cases (`case:S01`-`S03`). Point

runs, as on the arena. The first line it prints says which.

Its supplier is a deliberately plain script and **not** how the arena's suppliers behave: it opens
10 % above your current price, concedes a fixed 2 % per term sheet down to 90 %, agrees when you
meet its price, sends a final offer from round 5 and walks if you push after that; cited data is
only checked for existence. **The simulator teaches the contract; the real suppliers think for
themselves** - practise against them in the hosted arena and its sandbox (`--set sandbox`). We
don't hand out our suppliers: for a local opponent, build your own supplier simulator from the
public data - how would a foundry owner with a full order book answer your e-mail?

tests against it; set `ARENA_TEST_URL` and `ARENA_TEST_KEY` to run them against a hosted arena too.

A local, read-only MCP server (stdio) lets an MCP-capable agent or chat client explore the data
package itself. Six tools: `list_tables`, `query` (SELECT only, max 200 rows), `lookup` (the fact
behind a citable ID), `list_ids` (e.g. every month of one index series), `read_document`,
`get_case`.

```bash
claude mcp add arena-data -- uv run --directory /path/to/starter-kit arena mcp --data /path/to/data/package
```

or any client with an `mcpServers` config:

```json
{"mcpServers": {"arena-data": {"command": "uv", "args": ["run", "--directory", "/path/to/starter-kit",
  "arena", "mcp", "--data", "/path/to/data/package"]}}}
```

  `play()` reads the supplier's answer and goes on.

  ended, or you were late.

plus the Sunday release (new news, letters and a memo) once you have downloaded it."""

import csv
import json
import os
import sqlite3
from functools import cached_property
from pathlib import Path

MAX_ROWS = 200
RELEASE = "release-sunday"


class DataPackage:
    def __init__(self, root, release=None):
        """`root`: the unpacked package. `release`: the unpacked Sunday release (default: a
        `release-sunday` folder inside or next to the package, or ARENA_RELEASE), if present."""
        self.root = Path(root).expanduser().resolve()
        # facts.json holds every citable fact with the fields the arena checks claims against.
        own = self.root / "facts.json"
        facts = [own] if own.is_file() else [p for p in sorted(self.root.rglob("facts.json")) if RELEASE not in p.parts]
        self.facts = json.loads(facts[0].read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if facts else {}
        release = release or os.environ.get("ARENA_RELEASE")
        candidates = [Path(release).expanduser()] if release else [self.root / RELEASE, self.root.parent / RELEASE]
        self.release = next((p.resolve() for p in candidates if (p / "facts.json").is_file()), None)
        if self.release:  # new IDs only: nothing in the package changes
            self.facts |= json.loads((self.release / "facts.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        dbs = sorted(self.root.rglob("*.sqlite")) + sorted(self.root.rglob("*.db"))
        if not dbs and not facts:
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"no facts.json or .sqlite under {self.root}")
        self.db = None
        if dbs:
            self.db = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{dbs[0]}?mode=ro", uri=True, check_same_thread=False)
            self.db.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
            self.db.execute("PRAGMA query_only = ON")

    def tables(self):
        """{table: {"columns": [...], "rows": n}}"""
        if self.db is None:
            return {}
        names = [r[0] for r in self.db.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' ORDER BY name")]
        return {
            t: {
                "columns": [f"{c[1]} {c[2]}".strip() for c in self.db.execute(f'PRAGMA table_info("{t}")')],
                "rows": self.db.execute(f'SELECT count(*) FROM "{t}"').fetchone()[0],
            }
            for t in names
        }

    def query(self, sql, params=(), limit=MAX_ROWS):
        if self.db is None:
            raise ValueError("this package has no SQLite file")
        if sql.lstrip().split(None, 1)[0].lower() not in {"select", "with"}:
            raise ValueError("read-only: SELECT or WITH statements only")
        cur = self.db.execute(sql, params)
        return [dict(r) for r in cur.fetchmany(limit)]

    @cached_property
    def _ids(self):
        # A table's citable ID sits in its `id` column, else in its first column.
        index = {}
        for t, meta in self.tables().items():
            cols = [c.split()[0] for c in meta["columns"]]
            key = "id" if "id" in cols else cols[0]
            for row in self.db.execute(f'SELECT * FROM "{t}"'):
                value = row[key]
                if isinstance(value, str) and ":" in value:
                    index[value] = {"table": t, **dict(row)}
        for path in sorted(self.release.glob("data/*.csv")) if self.release else []:  # not in the SQLite
            with path.open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
                for row in csv.DictReader(f):
                    index[row["id"]] = {"table": path.stem, **row, "root": str(self.release)}
        return index

    def lookup(self, ref):
        """The fact behind a citable ID (from facts.json, else its table row), or None."""
        return self.facts.get(ref) or self._ids.get(ref)

    def ids(self, prefix):
        """All citable IDs starting with `prefix`, sorted, e.g. ids("idx:GP19-245113@")."""
        return sorted(i for i in self.facts.keys() | self._ids.keys() if i.startswith(prefix))

    def document(self, ref):
        """A document's text by ID (row with a path or body column) or by path in the package."""
        row, base = self._ids.get(ref) or self.facts.get(ref), self.root
        if row:
            for col in ("body", "text", "content"):
                if row.get(col):
                    return row[col]
            base = Path(row.get("root") or self.root)
            ref = next((row[c] for c in ("path", "file") if row.get(c)), None)
            if ref is None:
                return json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False)
        path = (base / ref).resolve()
        if not path.is_relative_to(base) or not path.is_file():
            raise FileNotFoundError(ref)
        return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    @cached_property
    def cases(self):
        """Practice (and demo) case files in the package: {case_id: case}."""
        out = {}
        for p in sorted(self.root.rglob("cases/**/*.json")):
            case = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            if isinstance(case, dict) and "case_id" in case:
                out[case["case_id"]] = case
        return out

This directory is the team's Python 3.12 project. Keep new negotiation agents in
`agents/`, experiment configuration in `configs/`, and execution infrastructure
in `arena_kit/harness/`. The original starter-kit helpers remain in `arena_kit/`.

## Install and check

Run these commands from this directory:

```bash
uv sync --frozen --extra sim --group dev
uv run --frozen arena-harness doctor
uv run --frozen arena-harness agents check --agent example
uv run --frozen arena-harness run --agent baseline
```

This uses the local simulator and makes no external Arena or model calls. Keys
in the environment do not enable a hosted run. The harness does not load `.env`.

## Develop an agent

```bash
cp agents/example.py agents/my_agent.py
cp configs/baseline.toml configs/my_agent.toml
```

Set `agent = "my_agent"` in the copied configuration. Implement `Agent.prepare`
and `Agent.decide`, then check and run it:

```bash
uv run --frozen arena-harness agents check --agent my_agent
uv run --frozen arena-harness run --config configs/my_agent.toml
uv run --frozen arena-harness compare RUN_A RUN_B
```

`baseline.toml` selects one case for a short experiment; the CLI without a config
plays all three simulator cases. Use `--max-cases 3` to compare all three with
your configuration. Compare matching case selections and data versions.

Use `services.data`, `services.cost` and `services.complete` for shared data,
cost calculation and budgeted model access. Keep state in the JSON returned by
the agent. Each teammate can add an agent/config pair without changing the
scheduler or transport.

## Navigation

| Location | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`HARNESS.md`](HARNESS.md) | Agent contract, CLI options, model limits, final start and recovery |
| [`agents/example.py`](agents/example.py) | Copyable team-agent example |
| [`configs/`](configs/) | Per-experiment TOML; no keys |
| [`arena_kit/harness/`](arena_kit/harness/) | Scheduler, transport, workers, journal, validation and reports |
| [`arena_kit/`](arena_kit/) | Reusable cost, data, document and simulator helpers |
| [`tests/`](tests/) | Local contract and failure tests |
| [`REFERENCE.md`](REFERENCE.md) | Original library/CLI examples, index argument example and MCP setup |
| [`../brief/api.md`](../brief/api.md) | Official Arena protocol |
| [`../data/README.md`](../data/README.md) | Official procurement data package |

## Validate changes

```bash
uv run --frozen pytest -q
uv run --frozen ruff check arena_kit/harness agents tests
uv run --frozen ruff format --check arena_kit/harness agents tests/test_harness.py
```

Default tests block external connections. Hosted tests and hosted smoke runs
need explicit authorization; follow [HARNESS.md](HARNESS.md) for those commands.
The Dockerfile serves the original local simulator; use the Python/uv setup
above for the full harness and team agents.

We are building buyer agents for the Tacto negotiation challenge. The harness
runs local experiments, compares agents and coordinates the live final. Start
locally, then select a hosted profile only when that run is authorized.

## Start locally

You need Git, Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). After cloning this
repository, run:

```bash
cd starter-kit
uv sync --frozen --extra sim --group dev
uv run --frozen arena-harness doctor
uv run --frozen arena-harness run --agent baseline
```

The default runs three scripted simulator cases with no external Arena or model
calls. Results, journals and reports go to the ignored `.runs/` directory at the
repo root. Simulator scores help compare local behavior; they do not predict
performance against live suppliers.

## Where to work

| Location | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`starter-kit/agents/`](starter-kit/agents/) | **Team agents:** copy `example.py` and implement your approach |
| [`starter-kit/configs/`](starter-kit/configs/) | **Experiment settings:** agent, parameters, model and limits; no keys |
| [`starter-kit/arena_kit/harness/`](starter-kit/arena_kit/harness/) | **Shared infrastructure:** API communication, execution, recovery and reporting |
| [`starter-kit/arena_kit/`](starter-kit/arena_kit/) | Existing cost calculation, data access, document parsing and simulator |
| [`starter-kit/tests/`](starter-kit/tests/) | Local tests; hosted tests require explicit selection |
| [`brief/`](brief/) | Official challenge, API and submission requirements |
| [`data/`](data/) | Official procurement data, facts, SQLite, contracts and notes |
| [`example_inputs/`](example_inputs/) | Recorded simulator inputs and attachments for inspection |

# Negotiation Arena — team harness

We are building buyer agents for the Tacto negotiation challenge. The harness
runs local experiments, compares agents and coordinates the live final. Start
locally, then select a hosted profile only when that run is authorized.

## Start locally

You need Git, Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). After cloning this
repository, run:

```bash
cd starter-kit
uv sync --frozen --extra sim --group dev
uv run --frozen arena-harness doctor
uv run --frozen arena-harness run --agent baseline
```

The default runs three scripted simulator cases with no external Arena or model
calls. Results, journals and reports go to the ignored `.runs/` directory at the
repo root. Simulator scores help compare local behavior; they do not predict
performance against live suppliers.

## Where to work

| Location | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`starter-kit/agents/`](starter-kit/agents/) | **Team agents:** copy `example.py` and implement your approach |
| [`starter-kit/configs/`](starter-kit/configs/) | **Experiment settings:** agent, parameters, model and limits; no keys |
| [`starter-kit/arena_kit/harness/`](starter-kit/arena_kit/harness/) | **Shared infrastructure:** API communication, execution, recovery and reporting |
| [`starter-kit/arena_kit/`](starter-kit/arena_kit/) | Existing cost calculation, data access, document parsing and simulator |
| [`starter-kit/tests/`](starter-kit/tests/) | Local tests; hosted tests require explicit selection |
| [`brief/`](brief/) | Official challenge, API and submission requirements |
| [`data/`](data/) | Official procurement data, facts, SQLite, contracts and notes |
| [`example_inputs/`](example_inputs/) | Recorded simulator inputs and attachments for inspection |
| `.runs/` (ignored) | Local run state and exports; no shared source code |

There is one Python project, with its `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` in
`starter-kit/`. Run Python commands there. New team agents belong in the outer
`starter-kit/agents/`; `starter-kit/arena_kit/agents/` contains the original
starter examples, exposed through harness adapters.

## Team workflow

Follow the [Python workspace guide](starter-kit/README.md) to add an agent and
configuration. Keep each approach in its own agent/config pair, run it locally,
and compare matching cases and data versions using `arena-harness compare`.
Changes go through a feature branch and pull request; commit agent code and
configuration so runs can be reproduced. Do not commit keys, `.env` or run state.

The harness permits one run per OS user and machine. Coordinate hosted runs
between team machines: they share the Arena key and quota. The original `arena`
CLI has separate execution and configuration; use `arena-harness` for team runs.

## Hosted runs and the final

[HARNESS.md](starter-kit/HARNESS.md) documents the full CLI, agent interface,
model limits, final start and recovery. Hosted sessions require `--allow-arena`;
remote models separately require `--allow-model` and configured call/output
limits. Keys come from `ARENA_API_KEY` and `LLM_API_KEY` in the environment.
Having a key does not activate a hosted profile, and the harness does not load
`.env` automatically.

Before the final, commit the selected agent, configuration and data, check a
clean checkout and use `--commit` with the full HEAD SHA. Start before the first
wave and follow the [final/recovery instructions](starter-kit/HARNESS.md#final-and-recovery).
The final runs without confirmation dialogs. Passing local tests does not
validate the live connection; perform a hosted smoke test only after explicit
authorization.

## Challenge and reference

- [Official brief and rules](brief/brief.md)
- [Official API protocol](brief/api.md)
- [Submission and pitch requirements](brief/submission.md)
- [Data package](data/README.md)
- [Original starter library examples and MCP setup](starter-kit/REFERENCE.md)
- [Upstream starter repository](https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit)

# Python workspace

This directory is the team's Python 3.12 project. Keep new negotiation agents in
`agents/`, experiment configuration in `configs/`, and execution infrastructure
in `arena_kit/harness/`. The original starter-kit helpers remain in `arena_kit/`.

## Install and check

Run these commands from this directory:

```bash
uv sync --frozen --extra sim --group dev
uv run --frozen arena-harness doctor
uv run --frozen arena-harness agents check --agent example
uv run --frozen arena-harness run --agent baseline
```

This uses the local simulator and makes no external Arena or model calls. Keys
in the environment do not enable a hosted run. The harness does not load `.env`.

## Develop an agent

```bash
cp agents/example.py agents/my_agent.py
cp configs/baseline.toml configs/my_agent.toml
```

Set `agent = "my_agent"` in the copied configuration. Implement `Agent.prepare`
and `Agent.decide`, then check and run it:

```bash
uv run --frozen arena-harness agents check --agent my_agent
uv run --frozen arena-harness run --config configs/my_agent.toml
uv run --frozen arena-harness compare RUN_A RUN_B
```

`baseline.toml` selects one case for a short experiment; the CLI without a config
plays all three simulator cases. Use `--max-cases 3` to compare all three with
your configuration. Compare matching case selections and data versions.

Use `services.data`, `services.cost` and `services.complete` for shared data,
cost calculation and budgeted model access. Keep state in the JSON returned by
the agent. Each teammate can add an agent/config pair without changing the
scheduler or transport.

## Navigation

| Location | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`HARNESS.md`](HARNESS.md) | Agent contract, CLI options, model limits, final start and recovery |
| [`agents/example.py`](agents/example.py) | Copyable team-agent example |
| [`configs/`](configs/) | Per-experiment TOML; no keys |
| [`arena_kit/harness/`](arena_kit/harness/) | Scheduler, transport, workers, journal, validation and reports |
| [`arena_kit/`](arena_kit/) | Reusable cost, data, document and simulator helpers |
| [`tests/`](tests/) | Local contract and failure tests |
| [`REFERENCE.md`](REFERENCE.md) | Original library/CLI examples, index argument example and MCP setup |
| [`../brief/api.md`](../brief/api.md) | Official Arena protocol |
| [`../data/README.md`](../data/README.md) | Official procurement data package |

## Validate changes

```bash
uv run --frozen pytest -q
uv run --frozen ruff check arena_kit/harness agents tests
uv run --frozen ruff format --check arena_kit/harness agents tests/test_harness.py
```

Default tests block external connections. Hosted tests and hosted smoke runs
need explicit authorization; follow [HARNESS.md](HARNESS.md) for those commands.
The Dockerfile serves the original local simulator; use the Python/uv setup
above for the full harness and team agents.
# Original starter-kit reference

This page describes the original `arena` CLI and library examples. For team
experiments and the final, start with [README.md](README.md) and use
[`arena-harness`](HARNESS.md). The two CLIs have different agent interfaces and
model configuration. The original `arena` runner does not use the harness lock,
journal or model budgets. Commands below that target the hosted Arena consume
sessions; LLM examples can also incur provider charges.

A Python client for the arena API, two example buyer agents that negotiate by e-mail, helpers that
read the suppliers' documents and price a term sheet, a runner that plays many cases in parallel,
`arena-sim` - a local simulator of the arena's API - and a read-only MCP server over the data
package. Read the brief first
(`../brief/brief.md`); the full API is in `../brief/api.md`. Code: MIT.

# Python workspace

This directory is the team's Python 3.12 project. Keep new negotiation agents in
`agents/`, experiment configuration in `configs/`, and execution infrastructure
in `arena_kit/harness/`. The original starter-kit helpers remain in `arena_kit/`.

## Install and check

Run these commands from this directory:

```bash
uv sync --frozen --extra sim --group dev
uv run --frozen arena-harness doctor
uv run --frozen arena-harness agents check --agent example
uv run --frozen arena-harness run --agent baseline
```

This uses the local simulator and makes no external Arena or model calls. Keys
in the environment do not enable a hosted run. The harness does not load `.env`.

## Develop an agent

```bash
cp agents/example.py agents/my_agent.py
cp configs/baseline.toml configs/my_agent.toml
```

Set `agent = "my_agent"` in the copied configuration. Implement `Agent.prepare`
and `Agent.decide`, then check and run it:

```bash
uv run --frozen arena-harness agents check --agent my_agent
uv run --frozen arena-harness run --config configs/my_agent.toml
uv run --frozen arena-harness compare RUN_A RUN_B
```

`baseline.toml` selects one case for a short experiment; the CLI without a config
plays all three simulator cases. Use `--max-cases 3` to compare all three with
your configuration. Compare matching case selections and data versions.

Use `services.data`, `services.cost` and `services.complete` for shared data,
cost calculation and budgeted model access. Keep state in the JSON returned by
the agent. Each teammate can add an agent/config pair without changing the
scheduler or transport.

## Validate changes

```bash
uv run --frozen pytest -q
uv run --frozen ruff check arena_kit/harness agents tests
uv run --frozen ruff format --check arena_kit/harness agents tests/test_harness.py
```

Default tests block external connections. Hosted tests and hosted smoke runs
need explicit authorization; follow [HARNESS.md](HARNESS.md) for those commands.
The Dockerfile serves the original local simulator; use the Python/uv setup
above for the full harness and team agents.
